subject: arts-and-music
unit_title: Advanced Studio Practice and Personal Direction
title: Launch and diagnostic: sustained observational and interpretive drawing
standards: Michigan Arts Education Standards: Visual Arts — Creating
essential_question: How does sustained studio practice turn a personal question into work worth looking at?
learning_objectives: Surface what is already known about sustained observational and interpretive drawing without penalty and establish the unit question.
Communicate understanding of sustained observational and interpretive drawing using subject-appropriate evidence or representation.
Check, revise, or improve the work on sustained observational and interpretive drawing against the stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task on sustained observational and interpretive drawing.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name a next step.
materials: sketchbook and course notebook or digital equivalent
unit-appropriate safe studio materials and tools
original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved reference works only

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a brief, accessible prompt on sustained observational and interpretive drawing. Ask the learner to notice, predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.

Observe closely, demonstrate the technique, let the learner work from direct observation or a developed idea, then revise from one specific criteria-based piece of feedback. Keep the work centred on sustained observational and interpretive drawing, name the success criteria, and model how to check the result.
Work through supported examples of sustained observational and interpretive drawing, fading prompts as the learner takes over. After each move ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that?”

Learner records current thinking about sustained observational and interpretive drawing — a prediction, a sketch, a first attempt, or a set of questions — before any instruction. Nothing here is scored for correctness.
Name one thing you already understand about sustained observational and interpretive drawing and one thing you want resolved by the end of the unit.

student_activity: Learner records current thinking about sustained observational and interpretive drawing — a prediction, a sketch, a first attempt, or a set of questions — before any instruction. Nothing here is scored for correctness.
formative_check: Name one thing you already understand about sustained observational and interpretive drawing and one thing you want resolved by the end of the unit.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for sustained observational and interpretive drawing, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to sustained observational and interpretive drawing works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of sustained observational and interpretive drawing, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: requests the answer to graded work
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking sustained observational and interpretive drawing mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use sketch or rehearsal record, created or performed work, artist statement, critique response, revision log, and portfolio reflection; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply sustained observational and interpretive drawing under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting sustained observational and interpretive drawing.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

study_integration.artifact_persistence: Persist a safe reference and metadata only: artifact type, learner-supplied title, family-chosen storage location, completion state, rubric evidence, and revision count. Do not store raw learner artifacts, media, recordings, or full project files in the study record unless host storage explicitly supports it.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one thing worth looking at more slowly, and record it in the sketchbook. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or private disclosure is required.

title: Concept model A: typography systems and hierarchy
standards: Michigan Arts Education Standards: Visual Arts — Creating
Visual Arts — Connecting
essential_question: How does design serve a real need without excluding the people who need it?
learning_objectives: Build a clear mental model of typography systems and hierarchy from an explicit worked example, demonstration, or source.
Communicate understanding of typography systems and hierarchy using subject-appropriate evidence or representation.
Check, revise, or improve the work on typography systems and hierarchy against the stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task on typography systems and hierarchy.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name a next step.
materials: sketchbook and course notebook or digital equivalent
unit-appropriate safe studio materials and tools
original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved reference works only

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a brief, accessible prompt on typography systems and hierarchy. Ask the learner to notice, predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.

Observe closely, demonstrate the technique, let the learner work from direct observation or a developed idea, then revise from one specific criteria-based piece of feedback. Keep the work centred on typography systems and hierarchy, name the success criteria, and model how to check the result.
Work through supported examples of typography systems and hierarchy, fading prompts as the learner takes over. After each move ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that?”
Learner reproduces the modelled approach to typography systems and hierarchy on a parallel example and annotates each step with the reason for it.
Explain the modelled approach to typography systems and hierarchy in your own words and name the step most likely to go wrong.

student_activity: Learner reproduces the modelled approach to typography systems and hierarchy on a parallel example and annotates each step with the reason for it.
formative_check: Explain the modelled approach to typography systems and hierarchy in your own words and name the step most likely to go wrong.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for typography systems and hierarchy, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to typography systems and hierarchy works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of typography systems and hierarchy, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: requests the answer to graded work
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking typography systems and hierarchy mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use sketch or rehearsal record, created or performed work, artist statement, critique response, revision log, and portfolio reflection; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply typography systems and hierarchy under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting typography systems and hierarchy.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

study_integration.artifact_persistence: Persist a safe reference and metadata only: artifact type, learner-supplied title, family-chosen storage location, completion state, rubric evidence, and revision count. Do not store raw learner artifacts, media, recordings, or full project files in the study record unless host storage explicitly supports it.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one thing worth looking at more slowly, and record it in the sketchbook. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or private disclosure is required.

title: Guided practice B: goal setting toward the concentration year
focus: goal setting toward the concentration year
standards: Michigan Arts Education Standards: Visual Arts — Presenting
Visual Arts — Responding
essential_question: What does a body of work say that any single piece cannot?
learning_objectives: Practise goal setting toward the concentration year with prompts, feedback, and gradually reduced support.
Communicate understanding of goal setting toward the concentration year using subject-appropriate evidence or representation.
Check, revise, or improve the work on goal setting toward the concentration year against the stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task on goal setting toward the concentration year.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name a next step.
materials: portfolio folder, box, or digital equivalent
documentation setup — artwork only, no person in frame
rights and permissions log; artist statement drafts

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a brief, accessible prompt on goal setting toward the concentration year. Ask the learner to notice, predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.

Curate rather than accumulate: select against explicit criteria, sequence for coherence, document accurately, and write about the work in plain language. Keep the work centred on goal setting toward the concentration year, name the success criteria, and model how to check the result.
Work through supported examples of goal setting toward the concentration year, fading prompts as the learner takes over. After each move ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that?”
Learner works two further supported examples of goal setting toward the concentration year under a changed constraint, with prompts faded on the second.
State how the changed constraint altered your approach to goal setting toward the concentration year.

student_activity: Learner works two further supported examples of goal setting toward the concentration year under a changed constraint, with prompts faded on the second.
formative_check: State how the changed constraint altered your approach to goal setting toward the concentration year.
topics_covered: goal setting toward the concentration year
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for goal setting toward the concentration year, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to goal setting toward the concentration year works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of goal setting toward the concentration year, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: requests the answer to graded work
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking goal setting toward the concentration year mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use sketch or rehearsal record, created or performed work, artist statement, critique response, revision log, and portfolio reflection; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply goal setting toward the concentration year under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting goal setting toward the concentration year.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

study_integration.artifact_persistence: Persist a safe reference and metadata only: artifact type, learner-supplied title, family-chosen storage location, completion state, rubric evidence, and revision count. Do not store raw learner artifacts, media, recordings, or full project files in the study record unless host storage explicitly supports it.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to choose one piece of your own work and say in one sentence why it belongs. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or private disclosure is required.

title: Unit assessment: foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation
standards: Michigan Arts Education Standards: Visual Arts — Presenting
Visual Arts — Responding
essential_question: What does a body of work say that any single piece cannot?
learning_objectives: Demonstrate current mastery across foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation, showing process or evidence for each response.
Communicate understanding of foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation using subject-appropriate evidence or representation.
Check, revise, or improve the work on foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation against the stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task on foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name a next step.
materials: portfolio folder, box, or digital equivalent
documentation setup — artwork only, no person in frame
rights and permissions log; artist statement drafts

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a brief, accessible prompt on foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation. Ask the learner to notice, predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.

Curate rather than accumulate: select against explicit criteria, sequence for coherence, document accurately, and write about the work in plain language. Keep the work centred on foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation, name the success criteria, and model how to check the result.
Work through supported examples of foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation, fading prompts as the learner takes over. After each move ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that?”
Learner completes the unit assessment covering foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation, working independently and showing process or evidence for each response.
Identify the item you are least confident about and say what would resolve it.

student_activity: Learner completes the unit assessment covering foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation, working independently and showing process or evidence for each response.
formative_check: Identify the item you are least confident about and say what would resolve it.
topics_covered: selecting and sequencing a cohesive body of work
presentation design for private or public modes
goal setting toward the concentration year
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use sketch or rehearsal record, created or performed work, artist statement, critique response, revision log, and portfolio reflection; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.
